Q6.raw_response:
Direct methods in optimal control are a class of techniques used to solve optimal control problems by discretizing the control and state trajectories and transforming the problem into a finite-dimensional optimization problem. This approach involves the discretization of the continuous-time optimal control problem, which typically involves a system of differential equations, into a parameterized form that can be handled by nonlinear programming (NLP) solvers.

The main idea of direct methods is to approximate the infinite-dimensional control problem by a finite-dimensional problem. This is achieved through the discretization of the time horizon into a finite grid and the representation of the control and state variables at these discrete time points. The control inputs and state trajectories are often parameterized using piecewise polynomials or other basis functions, such as B-splines. The resulting optimization problem is then solved using numerical optimization techniques.
